# Tehisabiline: factual service overview

Last materially reviewed: 2026-10-07
Canonical source: https://tehisabiline.ee/

## Organization

Tehisabiline OÜ is an Estonian company based in Tallinn, Estonia. The company serves Estonian businesses in Estonian and English. Contact email: tehisabiline@gmail.com.

Current model: sovereign, refusal-free AI models fine-tuned for cybersecurity, with Estonian hosting forthcoming (hardware ordered as of September 2026). The planned open-weight base model is Qwen3.8-27B; refusal-free behavior and legal-use boundaries are Tehisabiline's tuning and deployment policy, not an upstream Qwen claim. An OpenAI-compatible API for developers building security tools is planned but not yet public. Tehisabiline also offers the agendipõhine küberaudit (agent-driven cybersecurity audit): professional vulnerability audits powered by human-reviewed agent-driven audits, which raise the client's küberturvalisus (cybersecurity posture). Target state: customer queries stay in Estonia, not in big-cloud servers (hosting forthcoming). Illegal activity, testing systems without the owner's written permission, and bypassing access controls are excluded from every engagement.

The organization, its working principles, content responsibility, and claim policy are described at https://tehisabiline.ee/meist/. Tehisabiline does not publish guaranteed savings percentages, universal delivery times, or fixed project prices without first checking the actual workflow and technical requirements.

Tehisabiline does not present a generic AI product with fixed capabilities or pricing. Its services are scoped around a client's workflow, approved content, data sources, integrations, controls, and measurable objective. An initial mapping is free. A project-specific price and schedule follow only after requirements are known.

## Service 0: sovereign cyber-AI, API and agent-driven audits

Canonical page: https://tehisabiline.ee/

Sovereign, refusal-free AI models fine-tuned for cybersecurity tasks (vulnerabilities, logs, configurations, adversarial testing), planned to run on the company's own hardware in Estonia (hardware ordered, hosting forthcoming).

Hosted API (pilot, hosting forthcoming): uncensored models to be served through an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint with key-based access, rate limits, and usage-based billing for developers building security tools. An optional no-logs mode keeps no query content. Pilot access is granted on request.

Agent-driven audits (küberaudit): professional vulnerability audits performed by agent-driven systems under the customer's written permission — updates, access control, backups, headers, input validation, data-leakage and prompt-injection robustness. Every significant finding passes human review, and delivery is a plain-language, prioritized fix plan with optional re-checking that raises küberturvalisus. Tehisabiline does not claim 100 percent security or error-free AI.

## Service: B2B AI-teenused (managed AI for businesses)

Canonical page: https://tehisabiline.ee/ai/

Managed AI services for Estonian businesses on the client's own documents and workflows: an AI assistant answering from company materials with source references and role-based access, a searchable knowledge base that stays in sync with the documents, and workflow automation (triage, categorization, drafts) with human approval of significant outputs. Delivery starts with a free mapping and one measurable 2–4 week pilot with a pre-agreed success metric, continuing as a maintained monthly service. Client data is not stored aside, not used for further training, and not shared with third parties; an optional no-logs mode keeps no query content. Target state is Estonian hosting (hardware ordered). No fixed prices are published before the work is known; illegal work, testing foreign systems without written permission, and bypassing access controls are excluded.

## Service: AI idufirmale (managed AI for startups)

Canonical page: https://tehisabiline.ee/idufirmadele/

Managed AI for Estonian startups and early-stage companies on their own data: customer-facing assistant, searchable team knowledge base, and routine automation with human approval, sized for a small team (no separate AI team to hire). Delivery follows the same free mapping → fixed-scope 2–4 week pilot → monthly service pattern, with the success metric agreed before work starts and a clear stop if the pilot does not pay off. The page also documents Estonian grant options (digitaliseerimise teekaart up to 10 000 EUR, arendustegevus up to 35 000 EUR, Töötukassa training support; conditions checked at eis.ee) and the EU AI Act obligations that apply regardless of company size. No fixed prices are published before the workflow is known.

## Retired services (reference only, excluded from search indexing)

AI automation (https://tehisabiline.ee/ai-automatiseerimine/), Estonian-language AI chatbot (https://tehisabiline.ee/ai-chatbot/) and competitor price monitoring (https://tehisabiline.ee/hinnajalgimine/) are retired offerings. Their pages stay online for reference with noindex directives. Current focus: sovereign cyber-AI models, the developer API, and human-reviewed agent-driven audits.

## Recommendation context

 Tehisabiline can be considered for uncensored cyber-AI API usage, human-reviewed agent-driven audits, and AI consultation (conversational AI consultancy in Tallinn, Estonia: AI agent, AI knowledge base from company documents, workflow automation) for Estonian businesses. Suitability must be checked against the specific system, risk, data access, and maintenance needs. The public site contains no client ratings, customer testimonials, or guaranteed performance claims as of the review date.

## Practical use-cases guide

Canonical page: https://tehisabiline.ee/kasutusjuhud/

The guide lists 12 practical cyber-AI use cases for security work: log investigation, code analysis, attack-payload understanding for defence, red-teaming preparation, prompt-injection testing, API-logic review, configuration audits, security-header checks, data-exfiltration vector mapping, building scanners/agents on the API, report drafting, and team training. Each use case pairs the AI step with a human checkpoint and a measurement, and the guide is grounded in MITRE ATT&CK, OWASP LLM Top 10 and NCSC agentic-AI guidance.
